legend: Lateral radiograph of the right knee shows a mass containing punctate calcification and small foci of ossification at the posterior aspect of the knee. The mass is eroding the distal femur.
Sagittal T2-gradient echo MRI shows a hyperintense mass containing low-signal (calcified) foci.
Synovial chondromatosis may also arise within tenosynovial tissues (tenosynovial chondromatosis).
Higher-power magnification demonstrates the distinctive clustered chondrocyte growth of SC, with condensed lymphocyte-like nuclei and scant eosinophilic cytoplasm.

diagnosis: Secondary chondrosarcoma (grade 2) arising in pre-existing synovial chondromatosis (SC)
legend: A precursor SC is identified (top right) in this secondary chondrosarcoma.

diagnosis: Secondary chondrosarcoma (grade 2) arising in pre-existing synovial chondromatosis (SC)
legend: Permeative intraosseous growth infiltrating native lamellar cancellous bone of secondary chondrosarcoma arising in SC, with moderate cytological atypia.
Low-power histology demonstrates a lobular arrangement of hyaline cartilage growing in a striking clustered arrangement in a subsynovial location.
Classically, it is composed of multiple small nodules typically lacking a stromal vasculature.

diagnosis: Secondary chondrosarcoma (grade 2) arising in pre-existing synovial chondromatosis (SC)
legend: Rarely, a secondary chondrosarcoma may arise in the setting of a pre-existing SC. Note the intra-articular location of the SC and the permeative infiltrative growth of the secondary chondrosarcoma (bottom).

Synovial chondromatosis is a locally aggressive chondroid neoplasm composed of nodules of hyaline cartilage arranged in discrete clusters. The chondrocytes are small and lymphocyte-like with condensed chromatin and cytologic atypia is absent.

diagnosis: Secondary Chondrosarcoma arising in pre-existing synovial chondromatosis
legend: Secondary chondrosarcoma arising in pre-existing synovial chondromatosis centered in the sacro-iliac joint. Notice the intra-articular synovial chondromatosis which progresses into expansile sheets of malignant cartilage showing destructive and permeative intra-osseous growth and soft tissue extension.
